literal: Clothing, wealth, food, fame, learning, saying thus, all five, will not reach, gambling if one takes.
translation: Clothing, wealth, food, fame, and learning—all these five will elude one who takes to gambling.
modern: ஒருவன் சூதாட்டத்தை மேற்கொண்டால், உடை, செல்வம், உணவு, புகழ், கல்வி என்று சொல்லப்படும் ஐந்தும் அவனை வந்தடையாது.
explanation: This couplet lists five essential elements of a good life: clothing, wealth, food, fame, and education. The word 'oḷi' (literally light or brightness) is used here in the sense of fame or social respect, while 'āyam' refers to gambling. The poet warns that if a person engages in gambling, these five things will never reach them. Gambling strips a person not only of material necessities like food and clothes, but also of intangible assets like respect and learning.
